source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1933, p. 9 ("One contest foreshadowed in triennial elections: the list of nominations (23 ordinary members)"); Irish News, 11 May 1933, p. 4 ("Antrim Co. Council election: withdrawal (Slemish)"); Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1933, p. 11 ("County council elections: dates for counties Down and Antrim")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: 23 ordinary members (Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1933, p. 9: 'There are 23 ordinary members'), all returned unopposed; the sole nomination beyond the number of seats was Robert Gregg's in Slemish, withdrawn 10 May 1933.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received by Alexander Millar at the County Courthouse, Belfast, on 3 May 1933, withdrawals to 10 May, and a poll, if necessary, on Thursday 1 June 1933 (Belfast News-Letter, 22 April 1933, p. 11: 'If a poll is necessary it will be taken on 1st June'). The only threatened contest, in Slemish, ended on 10 May when Robert Gregg withdrew, leaving John G. Wallace returned unopposed (Irish News, 11 May 1933, p. 4), so no poll was held in the county. No party labels were printed. printed 'Edward O. Caruth' in the News-Letter and 'Edward O. Smith' in the Irish News; the Ballyprior Beg seat was held by Edward C. Smith in 1936 Returned unopposed.
